## What

A thorough audit of a real overnight fleet run (leader su-b2188 + 6 members on the p2p
plan, 2026-07-11→12) measured where tokens actually go — and the answer was structural,
not stylistic. Corrected per-session **model-inference counts** (assistant records in the
raw transcripts, counted with `jq` by record type): **leader 469 · L1 457 · L5 430 ·
su-3a43e 367**. The leader was NOT an outlier (early "leader 2.25× busiest member" was an
artifact — see the metric trap below). The dominant burns:

1. **A blocked lane live-looping** — one member spent **~367 inferences** waiting on a
   peer's critical-path work, waking, re-checking, and re-sleeping instead of parking on a
   gate event. Largest single avoidable cost in the run.
2. **Raw forensics in agent context** — a member piped `journalctl` / psql dumps / proc
   scans straight into its own context and paid **6 compactions in ~2 hours**, each
   compaction re-summarizing forensic bulk that never needed to be in context at all.
3. **The noise tax** — the leader's inbox crossed **9,500 messages**; multi-paragraph
   findings sent as coord bodies get truncated on injection, so long reports sent as
   messages are simultaneously expensive AND lossy.

### The metric trap (EI-9970)

The audit initially quoted `sessions:list`'s `turn_count` as "turns" — producing
incoherent numbers (leader "144 turns" vs members "19–64"). The owner challenged it;
recounting from the raw transcript jsonl showed `turn_count` was **the query WINDOW size**
(rows returned, capped by `limit`, default 40) — a pagination artifact, never a session
metric. EI-9970 fixed the surface: real units (prompt / response / tool-call counts) are
now exposed (migration 579). **Verify a metric's unit against source before quoting it in
an audit** — the entire first-pass ranking was wrong.

## Why it matters

Each burn class recurs on every fleet run if untreated: a lane blocked on a critical path
will always exist in a DAG-shaped plan; diagnosis lanes always generate forensics; any
fleet >3 members generates enough traffic that truncated coord bodies silently drop
evidence. On this one run the blocked lane alone cost roughly a full member-session of
inference (~367), and the forensics storm cost 6 compactions — both invisible to the
leader in real time because "alive and taking turns" looks like progress.

**Fault-ordering matters for the fix:** a member cannot park on a gate that was never
declared. The leader declaring the critical-path gate at kickoff comes FIRST; only after
that is a member's failure to bench/park on it a member fault. Judging member compliance
before the leader has declared the gate inverts the causality this run demonstrated.

## How to apply

Five rules now live in the su base persona (`su.md` — leader/monitor, coordination, and
discipline sections):

1. **Bench blocked lanes** — each monitor wake, bench lanes blocked-waiting >2 wakes
   (`fleet:bench { member, wakeEvent }`; `fleet:leader-brief`'s `benchSuggestion` flags
   them, EI-9943). A benched lane parks on the gate event; it does not live-loop.
2. **Declare the critical-path gate in the kickoff** (`events:emit { announce:true }`) so
   blocked lanes have a key to park on from minute one (fault-ordering above).
3. **Evidence-ordering for leader synthesis** — before proposing a mechanism or
   remediating a member-reported failure, re-read the owning item's checkpoint: ledger
   evidence outranks recalled hypotheses; and a member-reported TRANSIENT failure may have
   self-resolved — re-check the ledger before remediating.
4. **Findings >1 short paragraph go ON the work-item** (comment/checkpoint); the coord
   message carries a 1-line pointer. Inbox bodies truncate — the ledger doesn't.
5. **Raw forensics never enter agent context** — run them via `code:run` and return
   distilled evidence; park the evidence on the work-item. This is what turns "6
   compactions in 2h" into zero.

Plus two launch-time levers:

- **Fleet shape** — for a DIAGNOSIS mission, prefer fewer members: this run's evidence
  suggests parallel diagnosis lanes mostly serialize on one critical path while burning
  idle-wake inferences. **n=1 fleet-shape evidence — guidance only, not a persona rule**;
  re-evaluate after more runs.
- **Trimmed contextSize at launch** — members that only pull-work-and-report don't need a
  full-catalog context; launch with the trimmed payload tier where the mission allows.

### Peer-review amendments (accepted)

- EI-9939 (infra-liveness flap suppression) got an **ownership/routing leg** — severe
  events need a routed owner, not just suppression (**EI-10060**).
- The flap itself is a bug to root-cause, not weather — filed separately (**EI-10061**).
- "Fewer members" stayed doc-only (n=1); the checkpoint-first rule landed in the narrow
  "re-read the owning item's checkpoint first" form.
